note: The attacker-controlled fuzz input is written verbatim into the temporary .gpg file that GnuPG later parses.
Verification is invoked on the file containing the crafted bytes, causing the parser to consume the attacker input.
Signature verification drives the common packet-processing loop over the input stream.
Packets are repeatedly decoded from the attacker-controlled byte stream.
A literal-data packet is dispatched to proc_plaintext, which frees the current packet after processing.
The plaintext packet contents are read and used to update verification state before the packet object is released.
The plaintext packet is freed here, but the surrounding packet list still retains references used later during signature handling.
Signature verification later walks the retained packet list and dereferences packet nodes that may already have been freed and replaced.
The stale packet metadata is used in a memory copy, producing the ASAN heap-use-after-free read seen in the crash state.
